newsitem.title: CANADA: Commodity price pressures Canada energy stocks.
newsitem.headline: Commodity price pressures Canada energy stocks.

text.p: A drop in world oil prices was seen as the major factor behind a fall in the share prices of several Canadian energy companies on Thursday.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex closed down 79.13 points, or 1.25 percent at 6,237.09 in late trade. The decline outstripped a 22.58-point drop in the multi-sector TSE 300 index to 5,826.56.

Some of the large net losers among oils on Thursday included Talisman Energy Inc, down 1.40 to 39.75, Norcen Energy Resources Ltd, down 1 to 30, Crestar Energy Inc, down 0.60 to 25.50 and PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, down 0.60 to 55.90.
The TSE oil and gas subindex's drop, has concided with a fall in NYMEX West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices to below US$20 a barrel, a level unseen since the spring of 1996.
NYMEX crude closed unchanged on Thursday at US$19.47 a barrel.

Many investors, however, were unaware of the surprising recent strength in western Canadian natural gas prices, which was boding extremely well for the fortunes of producers, said Martin Molyneaux, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp.
Spot prices at the AECO-C Hub in southeastern Alberta, western Canada's most active pricing point, have climbed for two weeks as players rushed to inject gas for storage.

Canadian Gas Association figures showed storage levels in the west two weeks ago were 10 percentage points lower than at the same time last year, meaning that much more had to be stored before this year's winter heating season.
AECO gas for next-day delivery climbed to about C$1.80 per gigajoule on Thursday, up from about C$1.30 two weeks ago and last year. Summer prices have closely tracked spot levels.
"We've got a hell of a run before us to fill up the storage between now and November," Molyneaux said. "But nobody knows about it...everybody's focusing on oil prices."
